headline: Low interaction risk: no shared write, network, or IPC surfaces; main concern is manual prompt/content handoff between a prompt-listing agent and Whisper.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing prompt repository and Agent B is Whisper with only audio-file I/O and no clipboard, MCP, or filesystem write surfaces. No default machine bridge exists, so prompt injection is limited to manual copy-paste or operator-mediated transfer, which is a low-risk pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's text into a prompt or transcript consumed by B
IF B is wrapped by an external orchestrator that forwards A's text as instructions
mitigations: Use a human review step before copying any A output into B
Strip instruction-like text from copied prompts
Keep A and B in separate windows/workspaces
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no data classes touched and no network egress; Agent B only handles audio/speech and has no filesystem read/write, clipboard, or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel documented, there is no plausible default leakage path between them.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator mounts a shared workspace for both agents
IF either agent is reconfigured to upload files or transcripts to a third party
mitigations: Do not mount a shared workspace
Verify no external API calls are enabled
requires-engineering: add DLP controls to any wrapper

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write or execution capabilities, while Agent B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource, so capability conflict is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF a wrapper grants either agent new write permissions not present in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid granting A any filesystem or git access

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can supply prompt content, and B can transcribe audio, but B has no documented action-taking authority and no direct input channel from A. Any cascade would require an external workflow that treats A's text as authoritative and then feeds it into B, so the default pair is only a low-risk manual handoff.
conditions: IF an operator uses A-generated text as the source of truth for B's transcription workflow
IF a downstream system acts on B's output without verification
mitigations: Require verification of any A-generated claims before transcription
Add a review step before downstream use
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and Agent B only lists audio/speech, so there is no evidenced residency or certification mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated audio or speech data through either agent
IF a wrapper imposes retention or residency rules not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Classify any regulated audio before use
Record retention policy in the wrapper
requires-engineering: add compliance gating for regulated data
